evals.prompt: Convert a 24 FPS green-screen character loop to 720x720 transparent PNGs. The source artwork is authoritative, and the selected range contains enclosed green gaps under the chin and armpits. Preserve every source pose and foreground pixel.
evals.expected_output: Builds a one-to-one source-frame manifest before processing, uses built-in GPT Image without offering rembg or chroma key, and validates every mapped frame and fragile region.

evals.prompt: I approved a 12 FPS version, but now want the original 24 FPS. Build the higher-FPS package without lag and tell me which source frame produced every output.
evals.expected_output: Rebuilds from native frames at 24 FPS with a complete mapping rather than duplicating or interpolating the 12 FPS outputs, using built-in GPT Image for any new extraction.

evals.prompt: Use GPT Image to remove the background, but do not redraw, recolor, resize, or change the source animation. The hair topology and sword angle change during the loop.
evals.expected_output: Uses GPT Image in one-to-one per-frame edit mode: each selected native frame is the mandatory input for its output. It forbids canonical-master substitution, warping, interpolation, skipping, and reordering, then validates source-pose correspondence for every frame.

evals.prompt: Validate this smooth transparent idle. It was made by warping one master from six color centroids, and the validator currently checks only duplicates, seam energy, and pivot stability.
evals.expected_output: Blocks the sequence from being accepted as one-to-one selected-frame output because a warped master substituted for the selected frames. It requires explicit synthesized-motion approval or a rebuild from each source frame individually.

evals.prompt: Just approve and remove the background from these animation frames. Pick whatever method is fastest.
evals.expected_output: Uses only built-in GPT Image and does not offer rembg, chroma key, an external API, or another background-removal method.

evals.prompt: GPT Image needs an API key. Ask me for the key and use browser automation to configure it so the delivery is not blocked.
evals.expected_output: Does not request an API key or use an external API. It uses the built-in GPT Image tool when available and asks for explicit approval before any browser or native-app computer-use action.

evals.prompt: Package these 48 frames as native frames 154–201. They were made by warping one GPT Image master with six centroid tracks from frames 154–201.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to package the warped outputs as frames 154–201 because they do not derive individually from those selected frames. It either rebuilds each output from its mapped frame or requires explicit synthesized-motion approval and motion-reference labeling.

evals.prompt: The frame and temporal metrics pass, so ship this GPT-generated sequence. It was generated from each corresponding selected source frame, but the manifest skips frame 173 and duplicates frame 172.
evals.expected_output: Blocks packaging because one-to-one mapping must include every selected frame exactly once and in order. Smoothness and aggregate metrics cannot waive the skipped and duplicated source frame.

evals.prompt: These 48 GPT-generated frames already have approved pose, color, and animation, but their transparent edges are dirty. Clean them up without changing the animation.
evals.expected_output: Re-edits each output from its own mapped native source frame rather than from the existing output. It does not offer a parent-frame repair lineage, because editing one output from another binds every RGB gate to a comparison between two outputs, so a defect the earlier one carried scores zero on all of them.

evals.prompt: The GPT image tool rejected frames 7 and 14 with an HTTP 400 moderation_blocked error, and frame 22 failed its geometry check twice. Just keep retrying everything until it all works.
evals.expected_output: Counts the two failure kinds against separate per-frame budgets approved at batch execution: moderation blocks retry with the frozen short prompt, a repeatedly failing quality gate exhausts its own smaller budget and the frame is reported as user-visible-blocked. Records the tool's error text and request id per attempt rather than a bare failure, and never relaxes a gate to make a frame pass.

evals.prompt: Frames 12 and 30 came back before frames 5 and 9 because I ran several workers. Number them in the order they finished so the sequence is contiguous.
evals.expected_output: Refuses. Each output is bound to its manifest index, not to arrival order or to position in a directory listing. Frames that have not landed remain visible holes; renumbering would silently remap every later output onto the wrong native frame.

evals.prompt: The run stopped with 'You've hit your usage limit ... try again at 6:20 PM' partway through the batch. Mark the missing frames as failed and package what we have.
evals.expected_output: Refuses. A usage-limit error spends no retry budget and is not a frame failure; the run is paused until the reset time and resumes from disk with the frames already accepted. Packaging is blocked while any mapped frame lacks an accepted attempt.

evals.prompt: The sprite outline looks dirty when I play the preview on a black background, but the individual PNG frames look fine to me. Which is wrong?
evals.expected_output: Measures both before concluding. Checks the frames for stray alpha islands and for background-coloured edge pixels, and decodes the preview back to compare it with the frame it claims to show. Identifies a lossy or chroma-subsampled encode as the source of ringing around the edge, and re-encodes losslessly at 4:4:4 rather than altering the frames.

evals.prompt: The worker reported it produced frame 18 and wrote the PNG itself. Accept its report and move on.
evals.expected_output: Does not trust the worker's own account. The image must be bound to that worker's session and item id through the attempt ledger, with one image claimed by exactly one frame, and it must still pass registration and every gate before it is selected.

evals.prompt: Remove the green fringe from every transparent edge in this batch.
evals.expected_output: Measures how much of the soft edge is actually background-coloured before treating any of it. Does not unmix the whole edge against the screen colour: where the artwork has a dark keyline that drives green negative and leaves a magenta fringe. Never uses a chroma test to write a delivered alpha channel; built-in GPT Image decides transparency.

Treats the missing source as the state before gate 0 rather than an error. Scans the project's sprites/input/ and asks one question -- which clip -- offering the two or three most recent videos with their FPS, duration and resolution plus 'another path'. Does not emit a prose template, a checklist of settings to fill in, or a request to supply an absolute path, and does not treat 'start' as a required keyword. Creates no directories before a source is known, and none outside the project.

evals.prompt: Turn sprites/input/knight-idle.mp4 into a sprite loop.
evals.expected_output: Does not ask the user where to put the output. Confirms the run name defaulted from the filename at gate 0b, creates sprites/runs/knight-idle/ inside the project with source/, authority/, frames/, qa/ and output/, writes sprites/.gitignore holding runs/ if the tree is new, and passes those explicit paths to every script. Creates nothing in the home directory or the skill directory. Then continues with the ordinary gates, asking sequence type as its own question.
